concepts.title: Stop-the-Line Gate and Authority
concepts.description: Two distinct mechanisms share the name: the mandatory AC/DoD precondition gate, and every agent's Andon-cord authority to halt work.
concepts.notes: institutional knowledge, no single source file | TWO SEPARATE MECHANISMS UNDER ONE NAME | (1) STOP-THE-LINE GATE: precondition on implementation agents (BE/FE/DE) — check the Linear ticket has AC/DoD; YES -> proceed, NO -> FULL STOP, route back to BSA/POPM; explicit clause 'You are NOT responsible for inventing AC/DoD'; gate owner listed as 'Implementer', blocking = YES | (2) STOP-THE-LINE AUTHORITY: every member human or AI may halt progress; sourced to Toyota's Andon cord | authority covers exactly 5 categories: architectural integrity, security concerns, maintainability issues, performance implications, scalability concerns | exercising it requires 4 steps: explain the concern with specifics, propose at least one alternative, document via ADR or #PATH_DECISION tag, post a comment on the Linear ticket | gate table lists 5 gates total: Stop-the-Line (Implementer), QAS Gate (QAS), Stage 1 Review (System Architect), Stage 2 Review (ARCHitect-CLI), HITL Merge ({{AUTHOR_NAME}}) — all marked blocking YES | enforcement is prompt-level only: .claude/commands/start-work.md carries the gate text; no hook, script, or CI check verifies AC/DoD exists | routing when AC/DoD is missing: @bsa

concepts.title: Role Collapsing and Independence Gates
concepts.description: Which agent roles may be merged into the implementer for small work, and which are independence gates that never collapse.
concepts.notes: institutional knowledge, no single source file | introduced by {{TICKET_PREFIX}}-499 | COLLAPSIBLE: RTE only — PR creation and CI shepherding may be absorbed by BE-Developer, FE-Developer, or Data-Engineer; use when PRs are simple, work is single-agent, or fast iteration is needed | NOT COLLAPSIBLE (independence gates): QAS — always spawn a subagent, never self-review, rationale 'self-review bias, quality enforcement'; Security Engineer — never self-audit, rationale 'security blindness, conflict of interest' | collapsed flow: Implementer -> QAS -> [Implementer handles PR] -> HITL | stated invariant: 'Quality gates are immutable. QAS and SecEng cannot be collapsed.' | policy is prose in 4 files; nothing in .claude/agents/ or any script detects or refuses a self-review | UNKNOWN: no source states whether System Architect Stage 1 may collapse into ARCHitect-CLI Stage 2 when one actor holds both — the collapsible/non-collapsible lists cover only RTE, QAS, and SecEng

concepts.title: Three-Stage PR Review
concepts.description: PRs pass System Architect pattern review, then ARCHitect-in-CLI architecture review, then human HITL review which alone may merge.
concepts.notes: institutional knowledge, no single source file | Stage 1 System Architect: pattern compliance, RLS enforcement, technical validation; exit 'Stage 1 Approved - Ready for ARCHitect'; explicit MUST NOT 'skip to Stage 3' | Stage 2 ARCHitect-in-CLI: comprehensive review, architecture validation, security verification, cross-cutting concerns | Stage 3 HITL ({{AUTHOR_NAME}}): final human review, sole merge authority, action MERGE | Stage 1 validation checklist has 6 items: RLS context enforced (no direct Prisma calls), withUserContext/withAdminContext/withSystemContext used, authentication checks present, pattern library followed, TypeScript types valid, error handling comprehensive | entry precondition: RTE has posted 'Ready for HITL Review' after QAS 'Approved for RTE' | merge strategy fixed to 'Rebase and merge'; squash and merge-commit both forbidden | docs/sop/PRE_PR_VALIDATION_CHECKLIST.md is a separate pre-PR gate owned by ARCHitect-in-CLI with sections Documentation Completeness, Code Review Requirements, Security Validation, Test Coverage, Linear Ticket Completeness, Workflow Compliance, Code Quality, Documentation Quality, Sign-Off | the Stage 1 checklist is written against a Prisma/RLS/TypeScript stack and does not generalize to the template's other declared stacks | DOC DRIFT: CONTRIBUTING.md's review requirements state 'at least 1 required reviewer approval' auto-assigned via CODEOWNERS — a GitHub mechanism unrelated to the three named stages; the two review models are never reconciled in any source

concepts.title: Round Table Philosophy
concepts.description: Collaboration model treating human and AI contributors as peers with equal voice, defined roles, and authority in their domains.
concepts.notes: primary carrier docs/guides/ROUND-TABLE-PHILOSOPHY.md (324 lines); restated in README, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md | founding quote: 'We work as a round table team that has 4 pillars of SAFe inscribed on that round table. It means something.' | 7 principles, each with an 'In practice' clause: equal voice, mutual respect, shared responsibility, transparent decision-making, expertise recognition, constructive disagreement, collaborative problem-solving | 4 SAFe pillars named: alignment, built-in quality, transparency, program execution | contrasted against the 'order-taker model' where AI has no agency, ephemeral context, and no defined role | 4 worked examples: agent disagrees with a spec, human overrides an agent recommendation, multi-agent collaboration on a payment feature, FE-Developer vs System-Architect conflict resolution | decisions recorded with the #PATH_DECISION metacognitive tag; the full tag set per CLAUDE.md is #PATH_DECISION, #PLAN_UNCERTAINTY, #EXPORT_CRITICAL | the same doc also carries the canonical stop-the-line authority definition and the evidence-requirements table, so it is the source for three separate methodology concepts | philosophy is normative prose with no mechanical enforcement anywhere in the repo

concepts.title: Evidence-Based Delivery
concepts.description: Nothing advances on assertion: every deliverable carries verifiable evidence attached to the tracker before human review.
concepts.notes: institutional knowledge; canonical evidence table lives in docs/guides/ROUND-TABLE-PHILOSOPHY.md | slogan: 'All work requires verifiable evidence. No trust me, it works.' | 8 evidence types by listing: test results (Always), coverage report (Always), validation output of {{CI_VALIDATE_COMMAND}} (Always), session ID (Always), screenshots (UI work), RLS audit results (DB work), performance data (Tagged), security scan for #EXPORT_CRITICAL (Tagged) | evidence attaches to the Linear ticket via mcp__{{MCP_LINEAR_SERVER}}__create_comment | gate: no ticket reaches 'Ready for Review' without evidence; enforced by QAS and team culture, not by tooling | POPM approval sequence: RTE creates PR with evidence linked -> CI passes -> POPM reviews PR + Linear evidence + spec AC -> approve or request changes -> rebase-and-merge | swimlane Backlog -> Ready -> In Progress -> Testing -> Ready for Review -> Done, terminal state Done | docs/onboarding/QAS-DAILY-WORKFLOW.md carries the QAS Validation Report template that is the concrete form of the evidence block | the 'session ID' evidence type depends on Claude Code session identifiers and has no stated equivalent for the Gemini, Codex, or Cursor providers

concepts.title: SAFe x AI-DLC Program Cadence
concepts.description: SAFe keeps hierarchy and gates while AWS AI-DLC replaces the sprint with the Bolt: an hours-to-days swarm exiting on evidence.
concepts.notes: added by GH#53; primary source docs/guides/SAFE-AI-DLC-METHODOLOGY.md (142 lines) | thesis: 'SAFe with its clock replaced' — SAFe supplies hierarchy, WSJF, role boundaries, DoD; AWS AI-DLC supplies cadence and the human checkpoint | vocabulary: Bolt (replaces the sprint, labelled bolt:0/bolt:1, exits on evidence not a date), Unit of Work (AI-DLC Feature = tracker Project), Mob Elaboration (replaces sprint planning; decompose, list unknowns, ask questions BEFORE code), Mob Construction, the loop (AI plans -> AI asks -> human validates business context -> AI executes) | 3 AI-DLC phases modelled as 3 milestones per project: Inception, Construction, Operations | fusion mapping rows: Portfolio Epic->Initiative, Epic/value stream->sub-initiative or project priority, Feature->Project, PI increment->bolt:N label + target date, Phase gate->Project Milestone, Story/Enabler->Issue, Task->Sub-issue, WSJF/Role/DoD->description + agent:* labels + AC/DoD | Bolts are LABELS not tracker cycles, because cycles floor at a week and are team-wide | Bolt exit requires all three: issues merged, gates real and green, evidence posted | 6 decisions that always route to the human: secret rotation and blast radius, security policy (CSP/auth/headers), which CI checks become required and branch-protection changes, dependency severity and fix-vs-suppress budget, any SOP exception, signing the DoD | 4 dependency-wiring rules: fix the gate before the fix it verifies, rotate before scrub, capture before alert, upgrades before re-baseline; chains usually root at CI hardening | anti-pattern: forcing an ambiguous epic into one Bolt relocates the ambiguity into the code — run a spike instead | worked example is a gate-integrity Bolt (lint ignores, CI `|| echo` masking, weakened type-check config) | DOC DRIFT: README says the method ships as a skill for 'all four providers' but .cursor/ carries it as rule file 03-safe-ai-dlc.mdc with manual activation, not as a skill

concepts.notes: MAP-CARD, cites source | 613 lines | prerequisites: Claude Code 2.1.0+, Agent Teams experimental feature enabled | authoritative for: what Agent Teams are, enabling them, the first-team quick start, mapping the SAFe workflow onto a team, team sizing, quality gate hooks, token cost, known limitations, troubleshooting, and running teams remotely via Dark Factory | 11 H2 sections | distinguishes Agent Teams from the two other multi-agent approaches: subagents via the Task tool, and background agents (headless sessions) | team lead is TDM or ARCHitect-in-CLI; teammates are specialist roles; coordination is a shared TaskList plus inter-agent messages, with SAFe gates encoded as task dependencies | enablement key name: CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS in .claude/settings.json | read it when: considering parallel multi-agent execution, or budgeting tokens for it | flagged experimental in every source that mentions it; team-coordination is the only skill absent from .gemini/skills/ | DOC DRIFT (code wins): its 'Spawning Teammates by Role' tables assign model sonnet to BE, FE, DE, DPE, QAS, SecEng, Tech Writer and RTE; on disk all 11 .claude/agents/*.md declare model: opus | DOC DRIFT: its Merge Queue Enforcement section mandates `gh pr merge --auto --squash` while CONTRIBUTING.md states 'NEVER use Squash and merge'

concepts.title: Day 1 Checklist
concepts.description: SSoT stub: authoritative first-day checklist taking a new adopter from clone through a validated first agent workflow.
concepts.notes: MAP-CARD, cites source | 622 lines; stated time estimate 2-3 hours | authoritative for: the ordered, time-boxed first-day sequence with pass/fail validation at each step | 7 phases by listing: Repository Setup (30 min), Agent Provider Setup (30 min), Tool Integration (30 min), First Agent Workflow (45 min), Validation & Retrospective (15 min), Agent Teams Setup (optional 20 min), Dark Factory Setup (optional 30 min); plus Troubleshooting and Success | prerequisites listed: Claude Code or Augment Code, Linear/Jira account with API access, GitHub account with repository access | read it when: onboarding a person rather than configuring a repo — it is the human-facing counterpart to docs/guides/GETTING-STARTED.md, the same ground organised by clock rather than by task | docs/onboarding/META-PROMPTS-FOR-USERS.md section 6 supplies the copy-paste prompt that drives this checklist

concepts.title: CLAUDE.md
concepts.description: SSoT stub: the project context file Claude Code loads automatically, holding commands, stack, and the pattern discovery mandate.
concepts.notes: MAP-CARD, cites source | 204 lines; the shortest of the six root docs | auto-loaded by Claude Code as project context, so its claims reach every session whether or not anyone reads the file | authoritative for: the development command table (all placeholder tokens), the technology stack declaration, the repository structure summary, the metacognitive tags (#PATH_DECISION, #PLAN_UNCERTAINTY, #EXPORT_CRITICAL), the pattern discovery protocol ordering, and project-specific implementation notes for auth, payments, analytics, and database | it is the file class the README's Knowledge Vault section warns about: an independent audit told developers to trust the vault OVER the project's canonical context file because the latter had silently drifted | read it when: checking what an agent already believes about this project before you tell it anything | nearly every value in it is an unreplaced {{PLACEHOLDER}} token in this template repo, so no command in it is runnable as shipped | DOC DRIFT: its pattern discovery ordering (patterns_library first) contradicts AGENTS.md (specs first)

concepts.title: SECURITY.md
concepts.description: SSoT stub: the security policy, reframing risk for a prompt-and-config harness rather than an executable application.
concepts.notes: MAP-CARD, cites source | 144 lines; footer Last updated December 2025, Version 2.0 | authoritative for: the harness threat model, the vulnerability reporting channel and timelines, and the in-scope/out-of-scope boundary | threat reframing table maps traditional risks to harness risks: code vulnerabilities -> prompt injection, dependency exploits -> skill/command misuse, auth bypasses -> agent boundary violations, data breaches -> sensitive data in prompts | 5 reportable classes: prompt injection vectors, agent boundary bypasses, sensitive data exposure in templates, hook command injection, documentation encouraging insecure practice | 4 adopter concerns: placeholder customization, agent boundaries via .claude/agents/ tool restrictions, skill content review, hook scripts in .claude/hooks-config.json | response timeline: acknowledgment within 48 hours, severity assessment within 1 week | in scope: all of .claude/, agent definitions in AGENTS.md, workflow templates, dangerous documentation; out of scope: Claude Code itself, adopter application code, third-party integrations, example content | read it when: reporting or triaging a harness security issue | DOC DRIFT: its Supported Versions table lists 2.0.x as 'Current release' and 1.x as deprecated while the repo ships v2.10.0 | DOC DRIFT: the 'Before Adoption' subsection's three shell commands are unfenced prose and the third runs together with the following '### During Use' heading, so the heading renders inside the command
